nations.name: Sappony
nations.lands: the High Plains Indian Settlement along the North Carolina-Virginia boundary, including Person County, North Carolina, and Halifax County, Virginia, as described by Sappony

facts.text: Sappony identifies traditional homelands in the High Plains Settlement across North Carolina's Person County and Virginia's Halifax County.
facts.evidence: Person County, NC and Halifax County, VA

facts.text: Sappony's timeline dates replacing the state label 'Indians of Person County' with 'Sappony' to 2003.
Sappony's governance page describes a council with one elected representative from each of the settlement's seven families.
facts.evidence: one elected representative from each of the seven families

facts.text: Sappony describes committees addressing education, cultural preservation and economic development.
facts.evidence: education, cultural preservation, public relations, and economic development

nations.name: Waccamaw Siouan Tribe
nations.lands: Bladen and Columbus Counties in southeastern North Carolina, near Green Swamp

facts.text: The Tribe's introduction places its communities mainly in Bladen and Columbus Counties, North Carolina, near Green Swamp.
facts.evidence: North Carolina counties of Bladen and Columbus

facts.text: The Tribe's history identifies Priscilla Freeman Jacobs as its first female chief, serving from 1986 to 2005.
Its government page describes a Tribal Council elected by the membership and an Elders Review Committee.
facts.evidence: members who are elected by the tribal membership

facts.text: The program overview describes elder-led, hands-on education and STEAM learning as aims for tribal youth.
facts.evidence: hands-on learning workshops conducted by elders
